nsa_5g_downgrade_risk.explanation: Primary backup USID_26 has 5G_cells=2 (not zero), so the strict NSA-downgrade flag is not triggered. However, USID_26's 5G capacity is significantly lower (2 cells vs USID_00's 6 cells, and no 3500 MHz band), meaning 5G NR users handing over to USID_26 may experience noticeably reduced NR throughput. USID_41 and USID_28 are better 5G alternatives if reachable. Estimated affected_fraction = (6/10) × 0.013 = 0.0078 — very small given USID_00's limited dominance footprint.

capacity_verdict_reasoning: All 5 backup USIDs have post_outage_load_factor <= 0.012 (well below 0.5 medium threshold), confirming no congestion risk regardless of which backup absorbs USID_00's small traffic volume

USID_00's total dominant area is only 50 pixels (1.3% of total) — the absolute traffic volume to be redistributed is small, making overload structurally unlikely even with lower-capacity backups like USID_26 (score 15.6) and USID_30 (score 15.6)
USID_28 (capacity_score 25.6) and USID_41 (23.4) provide high-capacity 5G backup for users in the eastern and northern portions of the dominant area respectively
key_findings_for_stage4: USID_00 is a 5G-dominant, 4-band macro with the highest capacity score (25.6) in the cluster — shutdown represents a net loss of significant 5G NR throughput capability from this geographic pocket
Primary backup USID_26 has only 61% of USID_00's capacity and a 4G-heavy profile — 5G users will experience reduced NR speeds but service continuity is maintained
The 24% hard coverage hole (12 pixels, no backup at all) is the dominant impact factor — attribute analysis confirms no backup cell covers these pixels, not merely an underserved area
